summary: 7 to 10 minutes. The creative vision comes before efficiency.
point: The story reads at about 9 minutes now. If it needs 15, we go to 15.

Martha stays for now. She's the village turning up with groceries, she asks "Do you still think about him?", and she says "A fresh start doesn't bring answers", which sets up the paper game. Fallback: one of the sons brings up their father at dinner.
Matheus options for the writers: a photo only, his voice only (warm so we miss him, or wrong so we fear him), a 3-second doorway figure like in *Get Out*, or a happy flashback shot at Eliud's place.
The possession look stays subtle: dark under-eyes and paler skin, like in *Obsession*.
The boys wear generic school uniforms with no logo, never a real school's.

summary: No signed forms, no child on set. 6 hours max.
point: Sesilia prepares three forms: parental/guardian consent, medical and indemnity. The crew fills in medical and indemnity too.
Forms are signed before filming. Kids' scenes go in daytime.
Silas covers first aid. The call sheet lists the nearest hospital.

summary: Plan the look now, source it on the clock.
point: Core props: empty boxes (from Checkers, with branding covered), empty photo frames, a closet from Jeffrey, groceries and tea things.
The family photo in the frame gets shot and printed on the clock.
Most of the wardrobe comes from Jeffrey's warehouse. Sourcing it is part of the challenge, and part of the BTS.
Idea to explore: wardrobe colours that tie into the marketing, a detail people only clock later (think *Us*).
Silas makes the mood board on the clock, including the poses he needs for the poster.

summary: Luka leads effects. Everyone brings the makeup they already own.
point: The main jobs are the possession look and keeping every actor's look consistent from shot to shot.
The makeup team sends a product checklist so people know what to bring.

summary: Mics and lights get the money first.
point: Everyone lists their gear by Monday. Shaq works out the gaps on Tuesday and reports on Wednesday.
Most scenes are at night, so lighting decides how the film looks.
Still needed: a slate (clapperboard), a backup drive, and one box to keep all the gear in.
Laptops: Silas, Sesilia, James and Shaq, with more offered. Count the editors first.
Luka brings the cameras and mics for social content.

summary: Our biggest gap. Horror lives or dies on sound.
point: We're leaning towards very little dialogue (think *A Quiet Place*), so sound carries the fear.
Whoever records the sound also edits it.
Gloria composes and supervises the music.
Phone audio done well can work, but someone has to own it.

summary: Card to two drives to the editors, and editing starts on set.
point: Eliud copies every card onto two drives, sorts the clips into script order with the director's chosen takes, and works from one dedicated computer.
Drives: Chichi and Susann. We have one 4 TB drive and need a backup.
Editors: Saneliso and René, led by Eliud. Shaq on colour. Susann sits in on the cut.
Once the 48 hours end, there are no more edits.

summary: Travis's budget lands on Tuesday. Equipment first, then food.
point: Travis receives all contributions. The first meeting floated N$50 to N$100 per person.
Food: pooled groceries, at least one home-cooked meal and a volunteer chef. There'll be coffee (a machine has been offered), tea, and energy drinks if the budget allows. Check the dietary sheet.
Transport: one pickup and drop-off point, and maybe a hired minibus.

summary: BTS goes up live during the 48 hours, as proof we really did it.
point: Susann and Eliud create the YouTube, Instagram and TikTok accounts on the clock.
On the BTS team, one person stays on set and one roams, filming prop runs, the clean-up and the naps on desks.
Take photos of the cast and crew for the poster and credits. Shoot in landscape.
Release: a trailer first, then the full film in January. A team screening comes first, then a public one at the College of the Arts.

summary: Small local businesses, and something real in return.
point: Sesilia makes the asks, and Susann decides what we offer.
Corporates take weeks to answer. A local restaurant or café can say yes in a day.
What we can offer: a free promo video, the team eating there, and credit in the film and on our socials.
